coding.rationale: Music switches off when the user leaves, stopping unnecessary playback while the house is empty.
Turning the TV off after 30 minutes with no viewer avoids energy wasted on unwatched playback.
Boiler and fan are turned off after 10 minutes without movement so the empty bathroom consumes no energy.
TV and lights turn off once a person has been out of the living room for over 5 minutes, cutting waste in the vacated room.
Interest in tracking consumption and low-price periods reflects an ongoing intent to manage household energy cost.
Cutting power after 1 hour of device inactivity eliminates standby waste from idle equipment.
When family is absent from the living room for over 20 minutes, lights and TV are switched off to avoid waste.
The outlet turns off once connected items reach 100% charge, stopping power draw past full charge.
With daylight outside and the person in the room, the shutter is lifted and curtain closed to adapt shading for comfort.
Once the entrance door closes and no user is detected, the entrance light is turned off so an empty entrance wastes no lighting energy.
Alerts fire if blinds stay open between 10pm and 7am, keeping the night-time window-covering state maintained.
When no one is at home, lights switch off so an empty house does not waste lighting energy.
Shutters close whenever the house is empty, keeping the unoccupied home covered against exposure or intrusion.
Motion-triggered lighting when the resident woke at night maintains safe illumination, preventing falls or injury.
Scheduled and activity lighting support the resident's relaxation and reading, maintaining comfortable illumination while home.
